title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to address unfair queuing and intermittent request starvation observed under mixed-priority/mixed-sequence-length workloads. Changes include a hybrid queueing discipline, age-based priority boost for long-waiting requests, per-tenant max-wait timeouts with graceful fallback, and several scheduler-level knobs for backpressure and KV-cache affinity. Motivation: In customer canaries and internal perf lab runs we saw p99 latency spikes and sporadic starvation where low-batch-size, latency-sensitive requests would wait behind heavy batches for extended periods. The goal is to preserve overall throughput while improving fairness and tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic. Design highlights: - Introduced a multi-queue scheduler (fastpath queue for latency-sensitive or small requests, deferred queue for large/batchable work) while keeping the existing continuous-batching internals unchanged. - Implemented request aging: requests accrue an "age_score" and receive a priority boost once they exceed configurable thresholds (config: scheduler.age_boost_ms). - Added per-request max_wait_ms with two behaviors: (a) immediate fallback to a compatible smaller/quantized model (if configured), or (b) force-exec after draining the KV-cache warmup window to avoid indefinite waiting. - KV-cache affinity hinting: scheduler attempts to group requests likely to share KV-cache state; affinity is a soft hint to the batch assembler to reduce cold-KV penalty. - Timeout and backpressure semantics: when queues exceed configured headroom, scheduler rejects or backoffs non-critical requests using a gradated policy to protect SLOs. - New runtime knobs surfaced in config: scheduler.queue_sizes, scheduler.age_boost_ms, scheduler.max_wait_ms, scheduler.affinity_window_ms, scheduler.backpressure_threshold_pct. Compatibility: All changes are backward-compatible by default. Default config keeps previous behavior except for improved fairness; operators can tune knobs at the deployment level or via the Redwood Console rollout config. If "breaking_change" is toggled true by operator configuration, behavior can change (not set in this PR). Testing & validation: - Unit tests for queueing logic and aging heuristics added. - Integration tests in perf-canary harness that simulate mixed workloads (short chat-turn requests, long-generation requests, embeddings) and confirm no starvation. - Canary rollout to dedicated pool with mixed customer traffic for 48 hours. Observed results: p99 latency improved by ~15% for latency-sensitive requests in mixed workloads; overall throughput drop <= 2% in worst-case synthetic mixes. We observed near-elimination of multi-second queue waits in canary. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag (continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2=false by default). 2) Stage canary on one dedicated pool with scheduler_v2=true and monitor p50/p95/p99, queue depth, KV-cache miss rate, and error rates. 3) Gradually expand to remaining pools and hosted region after 72h of stable metrics. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf tests - [x] Canary run (48h) - [x] Config knobs documented - [x] Rollout playbook added - [x] Feature gated behind config/flag Related work: ENG-2145 (scheduler fairness), ENG-2210 (kv-cache affinity). Links: internal perf dashboards, Linear tickets, and benchmark lab run IDs are referenced in the review comments below.

review_conversation: Diego Martinez (reviewer): Can you clarify how age_score is computed and whether it can cause priority inversion?

Aisha Patel (author): Age_score = min(1.0, (wait_ms / scheduler.age_boost_ms)). It's a soft multiplier applied to the base priority; we cap boosts and include a decay window to prevent inversion. Added unit tests to show no inversion in pathological sequences.
Lina Zhou (reviewer): KV-cache affinity looks promising. How does it interact with autoscaling (i.e., when batches are split across GPUs)?

Aisha Patel (author): Affinity is a hint at assembly time; if autoscaling splits work, assembler will try to keep affinity groups together but won't block. We log affinity cohesion metrics to monitor effectiveness. Added doc note on expected behavior with autoscaling.
Marcus Reed (reviewer): We saw a ~2% throughput regression in one synthetic test. Is that acceptable?
Aisha Patel (author): Yes — measured tradeoff is predictable and opt-in. We include a knob to tune affinity and age thresholds; default config biases fairness over absolute peak throughput.
Diego Martinez (approver): Looks good. Please ensure the feature flag is present and rollout steps are in the playbook.
Lina Zhou (approver): Approving after minor doc updates (done).
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduling fairness and starvation prevention. Adds configurable queueing knobs, request aging, per-request max-wait fallbacks, and KV-cache affinity hinting. Default behavior preserves compatibility and must be enabled via scheduler_v2 feature flag for rollout.
perf_summary: Canary: mixed workload p99 for latency-sensitive requests improved ~15%, p95 improved ~8%. Overall throughput impact <= 2% on synthetic worst-case. Queue-depth tail reduced by ~60% for fastpath queue.
